summary: handleFlush stamps the write-ahead net's PJ-181 `snapshot` flag from `isModelDirty(tab.id)` alone, so a restore-seeded write-ahead-recovery model — CLEAN by construction yet holding content disk never had (`netUnsaved`) — re-labels its own sole recovery copy as 'already durable', which resolveNoteContent then rejects as a stale snapshot and deletes.
silent_failure_scenario: A save fails (the .md momentarily locked by OneDrive/Syncthing/Defender). noteSession.saveUnchained's `setNet` has already stashed the composed content, the model stays dirty, the save-health banner shows. The app is closed (or crashes). Next boot, restoreSessionTabs (store.ts:3665) reads with `preserveNet:true`, seeds the tab from the net, and calls setModelDiskBaseline(id, trueDisk, trueDisk !== content) → the model is CLEAN with `netUnsaved = true`; the user sees their recovered paragraph. They now do the most ordinary thing possible: switch tabs, alt-tab away (beforeunload), or just close the app. NotePane.onDestroy/handleBeforeUnload → doFlush (NotePane.svelte:1043/375) fires with `dirty === false`, so NoteEditor.handleFlush takes the `!needsDiskSave` branch and calls `setWriteAhead(filePath, content, cursorPos, scrollTop, SINGLE_OWNERSHIP && !isModelDirty(tab.id))` — `isModelDirty` is FALSE, so `snapshot: true`. The setWriteAhead downgrade guard (store.ts:347-350) does not stop it: it only refuses when `existing.content !== content`, and here the bytes are byte-identical (compose of an unedited freshly-opened model reproduces its seed exactly — the same identity adoptDisk's echo guard relies on). The net entry now claims its bytes are on disk. They are not. The moment the user opens that note again, resolveNoteContent computes `staleSnapshot = wab.snapshot === true && diskContent !== wab.content` → true (store.ts:3061), rejects the buffer, and on the manual-open path (`!preserveNet`) executes `clearWriteAhead(filePath)` (store.ts:3082-3084). The failed-save work is now gone from the model (re-seeded from disk), gone from the net, never on disk — with only a `console.warn` that release builds have no devtools to show. The restore path is no better: it rejects the snapshot too and silently brings the tab back with the stale disk content. `hasUnsavedRecovery(tab.id)` exists to answer exactly this and is not consulted at this line.

summary: The write-ahead crash-recovery net is persisted to a single `constellation-wab` localStorage blob that is never pruned or size-capped, and the `setItem` that persists it is wrapped in an empty `catch {}` — so once the blob crosses the WebView2 per-origin quota, every subsequent net-before-write stash silently fails to persist, killing crash recovery app-wide with no surface.
silent_failure_scenario: NoteEditor.handleFlush's `!needsDiskSave` branch (NoteEditor.svelte:409) stashes a FULL-CONTENT snapshot entry on every teardown — tab close, visibilitychange, `{#key}` remount — for a note the user merely VIEWED, and `resolveNoteContent` (store.ts:3061-3085) only clears such an entry if the user REOPENS that note. Nothing prunes by age and nothing caps by size, neither the in-memory Map (store.ts:330) nor the localStorage mirror; `walkAuxStatePaths` (store.ts:774) only removes entries on rename/delete. On the Boss's ~7,824-note universe, browsing a few thousand notes at a few KB each pushes the blob past the quota (localStorage persists across restarts, so this accrues over weeks). From that point `localStorage.setItem(WAB_LS_KEY, …)` at line 360 throws QuotaExceededError and the `catch {}` at line 362 swallows it. The in-memory Map still holds the entry, so the running session looks completely normal — but the crash-recovery half of the durability contract (`noteSession.saveUnchained`'s `e.setNet(...)` BEFORE `await e.write(...)`, noteSession.ts:250) now persists nothing. The user then types a paragraph, the 1500 ms save fires, the write fails (file locked by a sync agent / AV) or the process is killed before it lands: the only copy of that paragraph was in the dead process's memory. On restart `resolveNoteContent` finds no net entry, serves stale disk, and the model is born clean — the paragraph is gone from screen, from the net and from disk, with no save-health banner, no `.conflict` sidecar and no journal line. The same swallow also silently disables the PJ-102c "Save a copy" recovery path for closed notes (`getWriteAhead` at store.ts:576) and the MIG-100 restore's preserved-net recovery. Secondary: `setWriteAhead` runs on EVERY debounced save and does a synchronous JSON.parse + JSON.stringify of the ENTIRE blob (lines 358-360), an unbounded O(total-net-size) main-thread cost on the save path. The hazard is stated verbatim in the type's own doc comment at store.ts:317 ("never pruned or capped, and `setWriteAhead` swallows a quota exception with an empty catch") and used there as an argument for not doubling entry size — it was never actually fixed.

Accumulation is confirmed by the codebase's own prior findings — store.ts:373 ("a merely-viewed note's teardown flush pushes its unchanged body here") and store.ts:3050 ("NoteEditor's teardown stashes one even when nothing was typed, and nothing clears it for a closed note"), with NoteEditor.svelte:415 stashing FULL content on every teardown.

MEASURED (not estimated) on the Boss's real universe E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge: 7,966 notes, 306 MB, mean 39.4 KB, MEDIAN 23.0 KB, p25 9.0 KB. The candidate assumed "a few KB each … thousands of notes … over weeks." At a median 23 KB note (~46 KB of quota once measured as UTF-16, before JSON escaping every newline), a standard Chromium/WebView2 5-10 MiB per-origin allowance is exhausted after roughly 100-230 distinct notes viewed — one or two ordinary sessions.

Mechanism the candidate missed, which worsens it: at the boundary the blob oscillates. Opening a note calls clearWriteAhead (375), whose setItem writes a SMALLER blob and succeeds; the teardown re-stash then overflows and throws. The write then fails (file locked by Syncthing/AV) or the process is killed. On restart the Map is empty, so the localStorage mirror IS the net; it has no entry for N. resolveNoteContent takes the `!wab` branch (3004) and serves stale disk; the model is born clean. saveHealth (store.ts:423) is an in-memory writable and is gone with the process, so there is no banner; no .conflict sidecar; no console line. Not APP-KILLER: the primary `await writeNote` durability path is unaffected, so real loss requires a second independent event (failed write or process kill). This silently disables the recovery net that exists for exactly those events, far earlier than anyone assumed. HIGH, at the top of the band.

summary: The same UNIQUE-collision shape on `note_embeddings`: `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO note_embeddings (…, cid_cn) VALUES (…, (SELECT cid_cn FROM note_meta WHERE path = ?1))` against the FULL unique index `idx_note_embeddings_cid_cn ON note_embeddings(cid_cn)` (search.rs:4254). reason:
The core mechanism is real and provable from language semantics, not inference. At orchestrator.rs:153 the cataloger worker is a SCOPED thread (`scope.spawn` inside `std::thread::scope`); Rust's scope has no detach and joins every spawned thread before returning, so the abstain value built at line 177 after `rx.recv_timeout` expires (line 160) cannot be returned until the cataloger actually finishes. `run_one_safe` therefore enforces NO wall-clock bound — the function's own doc comment (lines 130-136: "the original run_one_safe only caught panics, not hangs... recv_timeout enforces the per-cataloger budget") and the module header's "Architect §10 invariant 12: ensemble timeouts are bounded" are both false as shipped. Catalogers run sequentially (orchestrator.rs:73-90), so every over-budget cataloger's full cost is serialized into the caller.

The silent harm is concrete and does not need a pathological hang: whenever a cataloger legitimately exceeds its budget, its correctly-computed trail is sent to the channel and then THROWN AWAY (rx drops at scope exit), replaced by an abstain — after the caller has already paid the entire wall-clock cost. Pure signal loss with zero timeout benefit. The file itself names this class a "silent-abstain regression" (lines 206-212, the Linguistic/الخط العربي r6 fix).

Reachability, grounded in this repo's own measurements rather than the candidate's theory: embeddings.rs:414-420 records a MEASURED ~32s `run_embedding` on a large note, and wiring.rs:128-132 holds `state.engine` across it. A large note therefore blows the 2s Semantic/Linguistic budget by an order of magnitude. classifier_scan_start auto-fires at boot+5s under cece.backgroundScan='on_startup' (scan_job.rs:110-115), and the interactive path classifier_suggest_for_note is `#[tauri::command(async)]` (classifier/mod.rs:90), so it parks a Tauri async-runtime worker with the panel spinner running.

Silence is verified, not assumed: the only signal is the eprintln at line 174, and this codebase documents (search.rs:1432-1437) that Windows Tauri builds are GUI-subsystem so eprintln output "go nowhere"; devtools is dev-only per project policy. No `classifier:scan` error event, no `last_error`, no UI surface.

summary: The sky back-fill drives an in-memory cursor across batches against the swappable `state.db`, has no `federation_generation` guard, and `finalize` stamps `schema_versions.sky` unconditionally — so a universe switch mid-run can permanently mark a partly-built universe as complete.
silent_failure_scenario: Universe A is mid-sky-backfill (7,600 notes × ~2 ms + 50 ms inter-batch sleeps = tens of seconds of window). The user switches to Universe B. `invalidate_search_state` (search.rs:10745) sets `db = None`; `ensure_search_db_ready` then installs B's connection and calls `sky_backfill::maybe_schedule` again, which spawns B's own thread. B's `run` (sky_backfill.rs:102) does `read_cursor` → `ANALYZE` (seconds on a 234k-edge note_links) → `UPDATE sky_nodes SET stratum=NULL, maturity=NULL WHERE path > ''` (wipes ALL of B) → then re-reads the cursor at line 147. During that multi-second ANALYZE, A's still-running thread writes ITS cursor into B's `sky_backfill_cursor` row every ~50 ms (write_cursor at line 158). B's thread therefore starts its loop from A's far-advanced path, skipping every B note that sorts below it, drains, and calls `finalize` (line 456) which stamps `schema_versions.sky` and deletes the cursor with NO completeness check. `is_needed` is false forever after; Sky View silently renders that whole swath of B's notes with NULL stratum/maturity, and no error, log line, or user-visible signal exists. The sibling `note_body_backfill::finalize` and `props_reparse_backfill::stamp` guard exactly this (the latter's doc comment names the universe-switch race verbatim, 2026-07-24 inspection); `reconcile.rs:281` and `derived_heal.rs:191` take the `federation_generation_now` guard for it. sky_backfill has neither.
reason: Real, silent, and unguarded — but the reachable mechanism is simpler than the one filed. VERIFIED IN CODE: (1) sky_backfill::run (sky_backfill.rs:102-161) owns no connection; every phase re-locks the swappable state.db cell, and Phase B (:302-308, up to 1,000 file reads) plus the 50 ms sleep hold NO lock — so a thread parked there across invalidate_search_state (search.rs:10745, *db = None) → ensure_search_db_ready (search.rs:11166, *db = Some(new conn)) survives and re-binds to the INCOMING universe's database. (2) grep confirms zero federation_generation_now calls in sky_backfill.rs, while reconcile.rs:281, derived_heal.rs:191/211/228 and index_repair.rs:840 all take that guard. (3) finalize (:456-472) stamps schema_versions.sky and DELETEs the cursor with no completeness check, whereas props_reparse_backfill::stamp (:153-183) refuses to stamp when rows remain and its doc comment names this exact universe-switch race, citing note_body_backfill::finalize as the pattern. (4) is_needed's doc (:86-88) promises a cursor-row re-run trigger that the body (:89-98) does not implement — it checks only the version, so nothing ever retries. MOST REACHABLE FAILURE (no sub-ms race needed): SKY_SCHEMA_VERSION is 10 and has been bumped ten times (search.rs:41-73), so after any bump every universe needs the back-fill — A and B both pending is the normal post-upgrade state. User switches A→B mid-run. B's thread reads cursor "", runs ANALYZE, then UPDATE sky_nodes SET stratum=NULL, maturity=NULL WHERE path > '' (:140-144) — every row in B is now NULL — and starts batch 1. A's surviving thread's next Phase-A SELECT … WHERE path > ?1 runs against B's note_meta with A's far-advanced cursor; when A's absolute path sorts above B's it returns zero rows, so A calls finalize ~100 ms after the switch, stamping B complete and deleting the cursor while B has recomputed one batch of eight. Any interruption of B's run then makes it permanent — and the natural interruption is another universe switch, which NULLs state.db and kills B's thread with only a diag line. NOTHING HEALS IT: converge's sky family (converge.rs:294-301) only runs behind an armed crash marker (derived_heal.rs:109-124); index_repair's full re-read is user-initiated; the live triggers only cover notes written afterwards (index_repair.rs:415 states no code rebuilds sky_links). Result: a swath of B's notes carry NULL stratum/maturity forever, consumed silently by Sky View (cache.rs:1023-1049) and the Reviewer (review.rs:1346-1360, "0 if unknown"), with no error surface. The filed variant — B re-reading A's cursor in the gap between :145 and :147 — is a genuine but far narrower window, since B needs one lock acquisition while A must finish Phases C, E and D before its write_cursor. DOWNGRADED TO MED, not HIGH: the loss is a derived index, never the .md source of truth; A must be inside its lock-free phase for the entire None window; and the next SKY_SCHEMA_VERSION bump re-runs the back-fill and heals it. Fix matching this codebase's own precedent: capture federation_generation_now at thread start, re-check before write_cursor and finalize, and add a completeness check to finalize.

summary: Identical unguarded shape in the outgoing-link aggregate back-fill: in-memory cursor over `state.db`, no generation guard, and `finalize` stamps `links_outgoing` + `links_vocab` with no completeness check.
silent_failure_scenario: Same trigger as sky_backfill. `run` (links_backfill.rs:130) captures `run_fp = link_types::snapshot().fingerprint()` for Universe A, does the slow `ANALYZE`, then reads the cursor at line 176 — the window during which a still-live A-thread pollutes B's `links_outgoing_backfill_cursor`. B's pass then starts above its own head, drains, and `finalize` (line 447) stamps `schema_versions.links_outgoing` + `links_vocab` unconditionally. Every B note below the stale cursor keeps a stale/zero `note_meta.outgoing_count`, `outgoing_link_types_json` and `outgoing_top_rank`, and `is_needed` returns false forever — so the Living-Link badges, the Reviewer's fragile/derives-from lens and every outgoing aggregate read serve wrong numbers permanently, with nothing surfaced. A second, quieter effect: A's thread can stamp B's `links_vocab` with A's vocabulary fingerprint (the two universes have different link-type registries), silently marking B's aggregates as materialized under a vocabulary they were never built from.
reason:
Verified in the actual code, not inferred. links_backfill::run (links_backfill.rs:130-192) reads the cursor once into memory at line 176 and drives every subsequent process_batch against whatever connection state.db holds at that moment; it never consults federation_generation_now (grep over the whole file confirms no generation guard), and finalize (line 447) stamps BOTH schema_versions.links_outgoing and links_vocab and clears the cursor with no completeness check. invalidate_search_state (search.rs:10745) NULLs state.db and bumps the generation on a universe switch; ensure_search_db_ready (search.rs:11166) installs B's connection and spawns B's own back-fill at 11189. A surviving A-thread therefore runs A's cursor over B's note_meta and stamps B as done.

Decisive corroboration: this codebase has already confirmed and remediated the IDENTICAL defect in three siblings. props_reparse_backfill.rs:153-166 documents it verbatim ("a universe switch mid-run ... easily inside the 50 ms inter-batch sleep ... leaves Universe A's cursor driving a scan of Universe B ... the drained scan then stamps B's schema_versions, and because the stamp makes is_needed false B never gets its own pass"); note_body_backfill::finalize (line 193) and library_attribution_backfill (header line 21) both carry the completeness-check guard. note_body_backfill's header calls links_backfill.rs "the proven model" — the model it copied never received the fix.

Aggravator unique to this module: write_cursor (line 436) PERSISTS A's cursor into B's links_outgoing_backfill_cursor table (props_reparse's cursor was in-memory only). Because version_current(B) is false on a first-time pass, B's own fresh thread does not reset the cursor (line 170) and inherits A's path — so even B's legitimate pass starts above its own head. If B's root sorts lexicographically before A's, the first "SELECT path ... WHERE path > cursor" returns empty, both threads instantly "drain" and stamp, and every B note keeps outgoing_count=0 / outgoing_link_types='' / outgoing_top_rank=9 permanently. Nothing is surfaced to the user — only a diag_log line reading "[links_backfill] completed: 0 notes recomputed". No ordinary-boot healer exists: recompute_all_outgoing is reachable only via after_repair_run, heal_interrupted_walk (armed crash markers only, derived_heal.rs:109-112), after_mig108, and after_vocabulary_change. Reachable trigger: a release bumping LINKS_OUTGOING_SCHEMA_VERSION or changing the seed link-type registry makes every universe need a pass, and switching universes within the 5-20 s back-fill window on a large universe is an ordinary gesture.

Two corrections to the candidate, both narrowing it. (1) Its "second, quieter effect" is backwards: stamping B's links_vocab with A's DIFFERING fingerprint makes is_needed true next boot, which (version_current now true) DELETEs the cursor and fully re-materializes — that path self-heals. Durable harm requires A and B to share a vocabulary (common: both on the 8 seeds). (2) The candidate omits the db=None window: if A's thread takes the lock while db is None, process_batch returns "DB not initialized", run propagates it and the thread dies. Survival requires the entire None window to fall inside one 50 ms sleep. That is an accident of timing rather than a guard, so it narrows reachability without refuting it.

summary: Deleting a folder that contains a registered library removes that library's registration from libraries.json permanently, recorded only by an `eprintln!` that does not exist in a release build — even in the RECOVERABLE trash/system modes where the files themselves come back.
silent_failure_scenario: The user deletes a parent folder that happens to contain a nested registered library (e.g. `Universe/Areas/` holding the library `Universe/Areas/Field Notes`). `delete_path` runs with the default mode (`trash`/`system`), so the files are moved intact into `<root>/.trash` or the Recycle Bin — advertised as fully recoverable. Line 7518-7520 then calls `retarget_registered_libraries(&app, &path, None)`, whose removal branch (558-568) drops every entry under that root from libraries.json and writes the shortened registry via `save_libraries`. The only record of that removal is the `eprintln!` at 561, which goes nowhere in a release build — note the deliberate contrast at 573-586, where PJ-207 §15 upgraded the *failure* message to `diag_log` for exactly this reason and left the *removal* message behind. The user then restores the folder from `.trash`: the .md files are back on disk, but the library is gone from the sidebar, from every resolver and from `nested_library_paths`' exclusion set (so its notes are now re-walked as ordinary folders of the parent library and re-attributed there). Nothing on screen, in the journal, or in diagnostics.log says the registration was deleted or how to get it back.

Reachable: add_library's ensure_under_active_root permits a library at ANY depth under the root (mig108::norm_under), so `<root>/Areas/Field Notes` is legal and `Areas` is an ordinary deletable folder. Deleting `Areas` in the DEFAULT recoverable modes (trash/system — 'permanent' is no longer a user choice per store.ts:4981) moves the files intact to .trash/Recycle Bin, then unconditionally calls retarget_registered_libraries(..., None), which retains-out every entry under that root and writes the shortened libraries.json. The removal is recorded ONLY by eprintln! at line 561, which reaches nothing in a release build — the identical concern PJ-207 §15 fixed twelve lines below (573-586) by routing the FAILURE message to crate::search::diag_log, leaving this REMOVAL message behind. guard_no_foreign_library_under (445-465) refuses only for a LINKED universe's library, so an own-universe nested library passes silently; the confirm dialog (+layout.svelte:10249) shows the folder name only and never mentions the contained library; and no in-app trash browser exists (no restore_from_trash/list_trash/TrashPanel anywhere), so the user restores the folder in Explorer and there is no hook to re-register. summary: `toggleTaskReconciled` writes the note's .md through the write gate (watcher-SUPPRESSED, so no `library-changed` ever fires), yet two of its three call sites — this one and the calendar popover (+layout.svelte:2172) — send no `screen:note-saved`; the third (+layout.svelte:9813) sends one but only `if (secondScreenOpen)`.
silent_failure_scenario: SS open, showing note F (cockpit, split companion, peek pane, or an SS tab). In the main window the user opens the Tasks dock page (GlobalTasksView) — or the calendar popover — and ticks a checkbox that lives in F. toggleTaskReconciled flushes F's model, toggle_task gate-writes F on disk (tasks.rs:469 gate_rmw, which marks the path watcher-suppressed), main reconciles its own model via reloadTabsFromDisk, and Rust reindexes note_meta/FTS. Nothing tells the second screen: no broadcastNoteSaved at this call site (unlike NoteEditor's six sites and store.ts's navFlushEnv/runPostSave/resolveConflictMerge, which all emit unconditionally), and no library-changed because the write was suppressed. The SS therefore keeps rendering `- [ ]` where disk now says `- [x] ✅ <date>`, and its cockpit gauges keep counting the stale body — silently, for the life of the window or until some unrelated save of F happens to fire the one channel that is wired. The equivalent RMW wrapper resolveConflictMerge (store.ts:6082) does emit screen:note-saved with the comment 'second screen refresh', which is the pattern these three sites should share.
reason:
Real and silent, but narrower than filed — re-scoped from "index-divergence" to a cross-window display-freshness gap.

CONFIRMED mechanism (all verified in source): toggle_task (tasks.rs) writes through write_gate::gate_rmw → atomic_write, which calls watcher_suppress::mark(&tmp) + mark_with_parent(path) (write_gate.rs:256-257), so no watcher 'library-changed' fires; and toggle_task never calls announce_disk_write/announce_frontmatter_writes — the exact re-announce that universe.rs:2597 and sources/mod.rs:653 exist to provide for other gated (suppressed) writes. store.ts:1409 toggleTaskReconciled emits nothing cross-window. Of its three call sites, only +layout.svelte:9813 emits (`if (secondScreenOpen) broadcastNoteSaved(filePath)`, commented "Notify SS so it can refresh its panels"); GlobalTasksView.svelte:151 and +layout.svelte:2172 (handleCalendarToggleTask) emit nothing. SecondScreenPage.svelte refreshes note content only via onNoteSaved (u2 → adoptFreshDiskIntoSS), 'cascade:rewrote', 'library-changed' (u5), universe switch, or workspace restore — none of which fires. Reachable failure: SS has note F open in its own tab (SecondScreenPage:1391) or the peek pane (:1225); the user ticks F's checkbox from the Tasks dock page or the calendar popover; the SS keeps rendering `- [ ]` while disk holds `- [x] ✅ <date>`, silently, with no error, until F is re-opened there or an unrelated save of F fires screen:note-saved. This is the on-screen-content === disk-content invariant the Editor-Surface Gate names.

REFUTED parts of the candidate:
1. NOT index divergence. toggle_task runs reindex_single_note with an explicit non-swallowing error path ("Safety inspection 2026-08-01 — never `let _ =` here"); note_meta/FTS match disk.
2. NOT data loss. The second screen is read-only by construction: `const ssReadOnly = true` (SecondScreenPage:194, Boss ruling 2026-07-09), setDisplayOnlyWindow() at script-init, and NoteEditor.svelte guards every write/rename entry (lines 208, 285, 361, 449, 529, 674, 791). A stale SS model can never compose a save back over the toggle.
3. "Cockpit gauges keep counting the stale body" is only partly true. When the toggled note is main's ACTIVE tab, reloadTabsFromDisk updates openTabs[].content (store.ts:1373), which re-runs the $effect at +layout.svelte:720 that reads $activeTab.content and calls emitEditorPanels({..., content}) — so the SS cockpit does self-correct in that configuration. The SS's own NoteEditor tab mounts and peek pane do not.

Fix: emit screen:note-saved from inside toggleTaskReconciled (one place, all three callers), matching resolveConflictMerge (store.ts:6082) and navFlushEnv (store.ts:653) which both emit unconditionally — or add announce_disk_write to toggle_task, the Rust-side equivalent already proven for suppressed gated writes.

summary: `rewrite_note_sources_on_disk` sets `effective` and returns Ok unconditionally even when `rewrite_frontmatter_sources` took its "Malformed frontmatter — leave alone" bail-out (line 519-522) and changed nothing, so the caller mirrors values into note_meta.sources and clears the suggestion row for a write that never happened.
silent_failure_scenario: For a note that starts with `---` but has no later line-initial `---`, line 519 returns the content verbatim; gate_rmw still sees `Ok(Some(rewritten))` and reports WriteOutcome::Ok, `effective` is set to the recognised ids at line 696, and `sources_set_manual` then writes those ids to note_meta.sources (mod.rs:796) and DELETEs the suggestion row (mod.rs:797) — a false success. The mirror claims a classification the file does not carry, the review card vanishes, and the divergence resolves only when the next index_note re-derives sources from the (unchanged) frontmatter and silently zeroes the column — at which point the user's Accept has evaporated with no message. Same at mod.rs:1211 for content_type and at bulk_ops.rs:468, where `mirror_to_db` runs regardless of `wrote`. Rated LOW on evidence, not on mechanism: a full-file scan of all 20,236 .md files across E:\Constellation Universes found ZERO notes currently in this shape, so it is reachable-in-principle (any note whose first line is a `---` thematic break) rather than live today — worth closing in the same pass as the two APP-KILLERs above, since it is the same two functions.
reason: Verified in source, end to end. rewrite_frontmatter_sources (sources/mod.rs:519-522) returns content verbatim when the note starts with `---` but has no later line-initial `---`. rewrite_note_sources_on_disk (mod.rs:692-697) still hands gate_rmw `Ok(Some(rewritten))`, so write_gate.rs:664-680 — which only skips on `None` — atomic-writes byte-identical content, journals WriteOutcome::Ok and returns Ok. Line 696 then sets `effective = recognised(&ids)`, and since sources_set_manual already validated every id at mod.rs:754-758, that is the user's full requested set. sources_set_manual writes it to note_meta.sources (mod.rs:796) and DELETEs the suggestion row (mod.rs:797). Nothing errors: SourceReviewPanel.svelte:786's catch never fires and the review card is removed from the queue. The divergence is then erased in the wrong direction — index_note (search.rs:7559) calls extract_sources, whose extract_axis_values_raw bails on the identical condition (mod.rs:241-243), yielding empty, so sources_json = None and the column is silently zeroed with no message. No guard or detector intervenes: the PJ-207 reconcile drift check compares .md files to index rows and, per its own comment at search.rs:11578, cannot see a derived column that is stale against itself. Both siblings confirmed — mod.rs:1211 sets `effective = ids` unconditionally for content_type, and bulk_ops.rs is the sharpest form: its closure correctly returns Ok(None) for the no-op and the code even computes `let wrote = matches!(outcome, ...Ok)` at line 463, then calls mirror_to_db at line 468 regardless of `wrote`, mirroring both axes and clearing the suggestion for a write it knows did not happen. Refutations attempted and rejected: the write is awaited/durable but writes the unchanged bytes; no error is surfaced on any path; the only existing guard covers the write, never the mirror; and it does not self-correct visibly. Severity LOW on independently measured evidence, not on mechanism: I scanned the Boss's all-time test universe (E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge, 8,060 .md files) and found ZERO notes in the triggering shape, so it is reachable-in-principle (a note whose first line is a `---` thematic break, or an unterminated frontmatter block from a truncated write) rather than live. No .md content is lost or corrupted — the file is untouched; what evaporates silently is one classification act plus a regenerable suggestion row. Not an app-killer, but a real silent false-success worth closing in the same pass, since the fix is one line at each of the three sites (return Ok(None) on a no-op rewrite, and gate the DB mirror on the write having actually happened).

summary: The canvas's teardown save deregisters itself from the app-close flush registry and then fires an un-awaited write whose only failure surface is a component that has just been destroyed, so a failed or cut-off .canvas write is completely silent.
silent_failure_scenario: The canvas is mounted under `{#if showSenseMakingCanvas}` (+layout.svelte:1551 lists it among the mutually-exclusive full-page views), so leaving it destroys the component. User drags/edits canvas items, then within the 1000 ms debounce clicks another dock button. onDestroy (line 215) runs: `pendingCanvasFlushes.delete(flushPendingSave)` (line 216) removes this instance from the close-flush registry, the pending timer is cleared, and `writeCanvasNow()` (line 221) is fired WITHOUT await. Two silent losses follow from that ordering. (a) If the write rejects (the .canvas file momentarily locked by a sync tool / AV), writeCanvasNow sets `saveError = true` (line 188) — local $state on a component that no longer renders — and logs to a console the release build disables (feedback_devtools_dev_only). The in-line comment at 219-220 asserts the failure 'still routes through saveError', which is not true after destroy. (b) If the user closes the app while that un-awaited invoke is in flight, the `session:final-flush` handler's `await flushPendingCanvasSave()` (+layout.svelte:3286) iterates an empty Set — the instance removed itself one line before firing the write — so the close handshake acks (line 3288) and the webview is torn down mid-write. Either way the last editing run on the .canvas file is gone with no banner, no retry and no journal entry; the file is that data's only store (there is no note model, no write-ahead net, no save-health path for it), which is exactly why PJ-207 §15 added the close-flush in the first place.
reason:
Partially confirmed — the swallowed-error half is real, the close-race half is refuted.

REFUTED (scenario b, the registry/close race): onDestroy fires ONLY when the user leaves the canvas view ({:else if showSenseMakingCanvas}, +layout.svelte:9058); the module comment at SenseMakingCanvas.svelte:2-9 is correct that it does NOT fire on window unload. So at app close the instance is still registered and flushPendingCanvasSave() (+layout.svelte:3286) awaits it correctly. Hitting the empty-Set state requires leaving the canvas AND closing the app within the flight time of an already-dispatched invoke; the Rust close arm (lib.rs:775-804) holds CloseRequested and the ack is gated behind persistSessionNow() + flushAllForAppClose() + flushPendingSettingsSave() + flushPendingPropertyTypesSave() — several awaited IPC round-trips that comfortably outlast one small atomic_write. Not concretely reachable.

CONFIRMED (scenario a, the swallowed write error): the un-awaited writeCanvasNow() at line 221 sets saveError = true (line 188) on a component whose banner ({#if saveError}, line 367) can never render again, plus a console.error that release builds cannot surface (devtools disabled). The in-line comment at 219-220 ("still routes any failure through saveError") is false, and canvas.rs:91 makes the same false claim ("A refusal here surfaces in the canvas's save-error banner; it is never silent") about the validate_path_in_any_library Err at canvas.rs:92. The loss is NOT bounded to 1s: debouncedSave() (line 196) resets the timer on every mutation, so a continuous drag/edit run writes nothing; leaving the canvas fires exactly one write for the whole run. If that write returns Err — e.g. the Windows temp+rename atomic_write failing on a target held by AV or a sync client, exactly the class the banner exists for — the entire editing run is lost from the .canvas file, which canvas.rs:80 states is the sole copy (no SQLite mirror, no note model, no journal marker, no .trash). No banner, no retry, nothing on screen.

Severity downgraded MED -> LOW: the common path still persists (the dispatched invoke completes; teardown does not cancel it), manifestation requires an independent environmental write failure, and the close-race that carried most of the MED weight is refuted. Fix is small: hold the pendingCanvasFlushes entry until the destroy-path write settles, or route that failure to a surface outliving the component (journal marker / global error path), and correct the two false comments.

summary: Sky View's 'Compute Semantic Links' button invokes `read_file`, a command that is not registered anywhere in the Rust handler, and swallows the rejection into `content: ''` — so every note is embedded as an empty document and the resulting similarity links are meaningless, reported as a normal success.
silent_failure_scenario: User opens Sky View, expands the AI panel and presses 'Compute Semantic Links' (GraphMindView.svelte:1085-1086). `computeSemantic()` walks `nodes` in batches of 64 and calls `invoke<string>('read_file', { path: n.path })` at line 378. `read_file` does not exist: zero grep hits anywhere in src-tauri/src, and it is absent from the generate_handler! block at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:394-760 (the only registered readers are read_note, read_note_preview, read_note_title). Tauri therefore rejects every one of those ~7,800 invokes with 'command not found', and the `catch { return { id, name, content: '' } }` on the same line converts each rejection into an empty document. `computeSemanticLinks(noteContents, …)` then embeds ~7,800 empty strings and returns cosine-similarity pairs computed over near-identical zero-content vectors; `semanticLinkCount` and `engine.setSemanticLinks()` present them as real discovered connections. The progress label runs to completion, the button flips to 'Recompute', and no error is surfaced — the user is shown fabricated knowledge connections in a system whose entire purpose is connection-making. Two sibling call sites read the same content correctly through `read_note` (+layout.svelte:6294, :7615), which is what makes this a stale command name rather than a missing feature.
reason:
The command name is genuinely dead and the rejection is genuinely silent. Verified: `read_file` has zero occurrences in all of src-tauri/ and is absent from the generate_handler! block in src-tauri/src/lib.rs (registered readers are libraries::read_note / read_note_title / read_note_preview only); no fs plugin is installed (Cargo.toml lists only tauri-plugin-opener, -updater, -process), so there is no `plugin:fs|read_file` route and the bare unregistered name rejects on every call. GraphMindView.svelte:379's inline `catch { ... content: '' }` converts every rejection to an empty body. `constellation_embed_texts` IS registered (lib.rs:557), so the pipeline runs to completion: progress label finishes, button flips to "Recompute", the "{semanticLinkCount} connections found" stat renders (markup :1069-1094), and no error is surfaced anywhere. Reachable: Sky View → settings → "intelligence" tab (:1006) → "Compute Semantic Links" (:1085). So the feature silently does not do what it says.

However the candidate's mechanism and impact are materially overstated, which drops the severity from MED. (1) extractSummary (semanticEngine.ts:51) builds `${name}. ${text.substring(0,300)}` — with content='' the note TITLE still survives, so e5 embeds distinct, meaningful title vectors. The result is degraded title-only similarity, NOT "empty documents" or "near-identical zero-content vectors," and NOT fabricated noise; the pairs returned are plausibly related by name. (2) Nothing is persisted: graphEngine.ts:852 setSemanticLinks() only rebuilds an in-memory this.semanticLinks array and flags needsRedraw — no disk write, no search.db write, no frontmatter, no index touch. There is no source-of-truth loss, divergence, or corruption. (3) No freeze or leak: the reads are batched 64-wide via Promise.all and each rejects immediately, so the loop is fast. (4) The layer is opt-in and toggleable and does not survive the session.

Real silent false-success worth fixing (change 'read_file' to the existing 'read_note' contract used at +layout.svelte, and surface the read failures instead of swallowing them), but it is a per-session visualization-quality defect, not an integrity or availability event.
